highlights.title: Hemas: broker Buy vs site fair value
highlights.figure: Target Rs 39 vs fair value Rs 15.90
highlights.text: HNB Stockbrokers kept Hemas Holdings (HHL.N0000) at Buy with a Rs 39.00 target (price Rs 31.80) after a September quarter with revenue +17.0% but profit to shareholders −3.0%. This site's fair value is Rs 15.90 (buy below Rs 13.52), so the broker sees more than twice the value this site does: a big disagreement.

highlights.title: Janashakthi Insurance Rs 7.95 interim
highlights.text: Janashakthi Insurance (JINS.N0000) declared an interim dividend of Rs 7.95 (XD 4 Dec, paid 24 Dec), a 29.2% trailing yield on Rs 38.70; the share jumped 24.55% on 26 Nov. The site's analysis (21 Nov) noted no 2026 dividend yet and puts fair value at Rs 16.06, far below the price.

highlights.title: Market slips, foreigners buy
highlights.text: The ASPI fell 70.93 points (−0.33%) to 21,244.91 and the S&P SL20 0.21% to 6,050.18 on Rs 2.65bn turnover. Foreigners were net buyers of Rs 34.29M (bought Rs 105M, sold Rs 71M), led by HDFC and PKME; Dialog and CIC took most of the selling.

highlights.title: Rate hike likely the peak
highlights.text: HNB Stockbrokers Research says the CBSL's 20 Nov move (OPR +25bps to 9.00%, SRR to 3%) has made banks cut back lending while loan demand keeps rising, and expects 9.00% to be the peak with gradual cuts possible next year.

highlights.title: Record exports; spared new US tariffs
highlights.text: Exports reached a record $15.28bn in January–October (+6.03%), with October the best month on record at over $1.62bn. Sri Lanka was left out of the new US tariffs of 20–40% on 14 economies including China, India, the EU, Vietnam and Bangladesh.

research.report: HHL.N 2QFY27 earnings summary (HNB Stockbrokers, Capital Goods)
keyPoints: September quarter revenue Rs 37.8bn (+17.0% Y/Y, +31.4% Q/Q): Consumer Brands +18.3% to Rs 15.6bn (Twiga, bought in August, added Rs 1.8bn; +4.8% without it), Life Sciences +16.2% to Rs 18.4bn, Hospitals +19.3% to Rs 3.2bn (admissions +4.4%, occupancy 73% YTD).

Gross margin fell 315bps to 29.7% as input costs and a weaker rupee were only partly passed on; Consumer Brands absorbed most of it to protect volumes, and regulated drug prices awaited the NMRA revision.
Operating costs grew only 6.4%, so EBIT rose 6.8% to Rs 3.8bn (margin 10.1%, down c.100bps); net finance cost rose more than fourfold to Rs 249mn on borrowing for pharma channel stock.
A higher dividend tax lifted the tax rate to 39.8% (37.2%), so profit to shareholders fell 3.0% to Rs 2.0bn (EPS Rs 0.67).

Working capital rose to 23.9% of trailing revenue (16.0% a year ago) and, with the Rs 5.5bn Twiga deal, HHL moved to Rs 11.9bn net debt from Rs 10.3bn net cash in March. Buy and Rs 39.00 target kept, short-term outlook Neutral.
forecasts: Stronger 3Q FY27 expected: Sri Lankan school season plus Twiga's first full quarter during Kenya's school season
Life Sciences to use the NMRA interim relief first to recover past exchange losses of c.7% rather than raise prices further
Consumer Brands margins to recover partly but stay below FY26 because of Twiga's lower margins
risks: High channel and distributor stock may sell slowly, delaying the working-capital unwind and keeping borrowing high
High oil prices could prolong Consumer Brands' margin pressure
A court ruling for the NMRA could reinstate the pricing formula and limit Life Sciences' price recovery
catalysts: Atlas and Twiga school seasons running together should drive a strong 3Q FY27
Interim NMRA pricing relief should support Life Sciences' margins as past exchange losses are recovered
Proposed VAT removal on exercise books and a higher income-tax-free threshold should help Learning volumes and consumer demand

news.title: Sri Lanka left out of new US tariffs
news.text: The White House announced tariffs of 20% to 40% on 14 economies after trade-practice investigations, including China (up to 40%), Vietnam (up to 35%), India, the EU and Bangladesh; Sri Lanka isn't among them. Caps agreed by the US lower the effective rate for some.

news.title: Record exports in 10 months
news.text: Exports reached $15.28bn in January–October, up 6.03%: goods +5.72% to $12.01bn and services +7.2% to $3.26bn. October was the best month on record at over $1.62bn. The EDB now expects about 6.5% growth for the year, below its 8–10% target, because of Middle East-related costs.

news.title: SriLankan Airlines adds fuel surcharge
news.text: After a $35mn loss in the first half as jet fuel rose from $2.10 to $4.40–4.50 a gallon, the national carrier added a fuel surcharge and aims to break even by March. It took no fuel subsidy.

news.title: Port of Colombo targets value addition
news.text: The deputy minister wants each container to add $2,000–3,000 to the economy instead of $50–100 from transhipment, by drawing 5–10% of the 9 million containers into local value-added work; a Cabinet paper on a Colombo Port Logistics Hub is due within a week or two.

news.title: President wants land released faster
news.text: The President said tax breaks alone won't attract investors while getting land takes about 18 months; a committee discussed putting State land under the BOI or a land bank.

news.title: National battery testing centre opens
news.text: A Rs 161.5mn Centre for E-Mobility and Battery Technology opened at NERDC to test modern batteries and EV charging equipment: Rs 118mn from the government's quality-infrastructure project and Rs 43.5mn from NERDC.

news.title: Sri Lanka seeks RCEP through ASEAN
news.text: The ambassador to Indonesia repeated Sri Lanka's aim to join the RCEP trade pact via ASEAN sectoral dialogue partnership; Sri Lankan firms have invested over $1.3bn in Indonesia against little Indonesian investment here.

news.title: Rate hike reaches banks, not borrowers
news.text: HNB Stockbrokers Research: after the CBSL raised the OPR by 25bps to 9.00% and the SRR to 3% on 20 Nov, banks have cut back lending but loan demand is still rising. It sees 9.00% as likely the peak, with gradual cuts possible next year.

news.title: New US tariffs on 14 trading partners
news.text: President Trump announced tariffs over excess industrial capacity on 14 partners including China, Japan and the EU, despite his party's midterm losses.

news.title: Asian shares bounce
news.text: Asian markets rallied on Thursday after Wall Street recovered from deep lows, though worries about circular AI financing and the new US tariffs kept the mood muted in holiday-thin trade. At 09:10 Sri Lanka time the Hang Seng was +2.06%, TAIEX +2.13% and Nikkei +1.54%.
